newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease in week.

text.p: The Australian wool market eased at auctions in Sydney and Fremantle this week, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its market report.
The eastern market indicator fell eight cents to 607 cents a kg clean and western indicator fell 11 cents to 542 cents.
Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said the gradual upward trend was arrested this week and there was a generally weaker tone to the market.
Next week's sale is the first of a series of larger quantities available for 1996/97 season and it is anticipated these will dampen current prices, it said.
A total of 65,276 bales were offered this week with 16.7 percent passed in.
In the futures market, a total of 143 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended Thursday. The near October contract closed 19 cents down at 750 cents a kg clean.
Wool International said it sold 15,038 farm equivalent bales from its stockpile in the week to Thursday, leaving the stockpile at 2,116,751 bales.
The sold forward position is 183,323 bales for the September quarter and 69,196 for the December quarter, it said.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 101,023 bales on offer, the highest offering in 10 weeks.
